strategies.name: Direct Sequential All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Perform 16 dependent all-reduce operations sequentially, each with full vector (world_size*256 elements). Each iteration applies per-shard scaling, all-reduce, then inverse scaling. Results in exactly 16 all-reduce dispatches with maximum payload size but no fusion opportunity due to dependencies.

strategies.name: Chunked Independent Micro-Batch Pipeline
strategies.desc: Split the 16 iterations into independent sub-problems by partitioning the vector into spatial chunks that can progress through different iteration stages simultaneously. Uses pipelined all-reduce dispatches (still 16 total) but with smaller per-dispatch payloads and potential for network overlap across chunks, trading increased local computation for better interconnect utilization.

strategies.name: Fused Scale-AllReduce Kernel Batching
strategies.desc: Merge the scale-before and scale-after operations with the all-reduce by pre-computing combined scaling factors and deferring normalization. Reduces to 8 all-reduce dispatches by fusing pairs of dependent operations where the intermediate inverse-scale followed by forward-scale can algebraically cancel or combine, halving dispatch count at cost of numerical precision management.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter All-Gather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Replace each all-reduce with reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, allowing per-rank computation on local shards between the two phases. Results in 32 collective dispatches (16×2) but each moving only 1/world_size of data in reduce-scatter phase, potentially better for large world_size by exploiting bandwidth-latency tradeoffs and enabling local computation parallelism.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Aggregation
strategies.desc:
Exploit multi-node topology by performing intra-node all-reduce (assuming multiple devices per node) followed by inter-node all-reduce for each of the 16 iterations. Requires 32 dispatches (16 intra-node + 16 inter-node) but with drastically smaller world-sizes per collective, reducing algorithmic complexity from O(W) to O(W/nodes + nodes) and better utilizing node-local interconnect bandwidth.
